terms.label: Contact and magnetic force
terms.plain: A magnet can change how strongly an object presses on a balance.
terms.meaning: N is upward contact force; Fm is the stipulated upward magnetic force and mg the downward weight.
cautions: A smaller contact reading does not establish changed gravity; N the variable differs from N the unit.

terms.label: Mass and gravitational acceleration
terms.plain: Mass and gravitational acceleration together determine weight.
terms.meaning: In the static comparison g is stipulated as 9.80665 m/s², not inferred from a balance change.
cautions: m as mass differs from m as the metre unit.

equations.title: Balance contact differs from gravity
equations.equation: N = mg − Fm, only while N ≥ 0
equations.plain: An upward magnetic force can reduce the balance contact force without changing gravity.
equations.convention: Static supported contact; external magnet reaction carried outside the balance.
equations.units: N and Fm newtons; m kilograms; g m/s².
cautions: The contact model does not apply after separation.

handbook.title: Magnet, balance and external reaction support
handbook.overview: Proposed geometry, not a photograph or quantitative magnet simulation. The external stand carries the opposite magnetic reaction; scale-field response and common-table vibration remain confounds. No gravity change or antigravity device is demonstrated.
handbook.goal: See where an ordinary magnetic reaction is carried, rather than treating a balance change as unsupported lift or antigravity.
signalSteps: Identify the magnet, supported object, balance and external stand.
Track which support carries the opposite magnetic reaction.
Treat shared-table vibration and instrument response as competing explanations.
